clue.text: Corrects the final part in a script

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the letters of the other, here inside a script

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten script
the end is the final part of anything

explanation.surface: An editor fixes the closing section of a play's text.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to correct it, so corrects is a present-tense synonym.

clue.text: Merchant who was in debt for a pound

definitions.text: Merchant who was in debt for a pound

parts.words: Merchant who was in debt for a pound
parts.note: the title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice borrowed money from Shylock against a pound of his own flesh

explanation.surface: A trader owing a single pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pound' looks like money but is Shylock's pound of flesh in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's merchant of Venice bears this name and pledged a pound of flesh as security.

clue.text: Macabre how corpse ends in the lake

indicators.note: ends here picks the closing letter of the word corpse

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A gruesome story asks how a dead body finished up in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is weird and frightening, close in sense to macabre or ghastly.

clue.text: Fed up with being exploited and rendered ineffective

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to be used is to be exploited

explanation.surface: Someone sick of being taken advantage of has lost their fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A defused bomb or situation has been made harmless, so rendered ineffective is a past-participle synonym.

definitions.meaning: in poker a bluff, a pretended strong hand, may be called by an opponent

explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is both a poker pretence that can be called and a steep cliff or headland.

clue.text: Get the member to finish an old story

parts.note: a leg is a limb, which is a member of the body
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: A storyteller asks a club member to wrap up an ancient tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story handed down from long ago.

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
a bill or billhook is an example of a cutting tool, with say marking the example

explanation.surface: Someone settles an invoice for a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pays bill' reads as one idea, but 'Pays' alone gives FOOTS and 'bill, say' gives TOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low piece of furniture to rest the feet on.

clue.text: Just one type of shirt or vest

parts.note: single means just one
T as in T-shirt, a type of shirt

explanation.surface: A clothes shop offers only one kind of top.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless undershirt, which British English calls a vest.

clue.text: Vigilant chap who never does a day's work

definitions.text: Vigilant chap who never does a day's work

parts.words: Vigilant chap who never does a day's work
parts.note: a guard who keeps watch through the dark hours and so never works in daylight, which sounds like an idler

explanation.surface: A watchful man who is nonetheless bone idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never does a day's work' suggests laziness but means he works only at night. In cricket the word is also a lower-order batsman sent in late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A night watchman guards premises after dark, so he works only through the night.

definitions.meaning: a heavenly body seen in the sky each night

explanation.definitionFit: A star is both a celebrity and a point of light seen in the night sky.

clue.text: You may have fun here for a pretty good cause

parts.note: fair means moderately good, as in a fair performance
a ground is a reason or cause, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A charity event that is fun to attend, all for a worthy cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is a site with rides and stalls where people go to enjoy themselves.

indicators.note: broke suggests the word Ernest is smashed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete called Ernest set new best marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, so records is a present-tense synonym.

indicators.note: round says one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: holy means good in the sense of saintly
a nest is a home, as of a bird

explanation.surface: A house described as reasonably good all round.
explanation.definitionFit: To act honestly is to act fairly, without cheating.

parts.note: an aircraft lands on its three sets of wheels, the moment it reaches the runway

explanation.surface: An aircraft settles on its wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-point' may suggest a score, as in American football, but the landing is a plane coming to ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching down is what an aircraft does as its wheels meet the runway.

definitions.meaning: a round of ammunition for a gun

explanation.definitionFit: Cartridge is a heavy drawing paper and also a single round of ammunition.

clue.text: Vessel has got right inside the harbour

indicators.note: inside says one letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

explanation.surface: A ship has made it safely into the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A port is a harbour town where ships dock.

clue.text: A Conservative leader about to give ground

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Conservative

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Tory leader concedes territory.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a measured area of land, a piece of ground.

clue.text: Difficult week in a hospital department

parts.note: a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient endures a hard seven days on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to handle or deal with, a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: Hope yet for an art form

definitions.meaning: there is ..., so there is still hope, as in while there's life there's hope
a painting of arranged objects such as fruit or flowers

explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a genre of painting depicting inanimate objects arranged together.

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespeare play
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone conceals an item in a theatrical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb meaning conceal but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal hide, so the noun hide fits.

definitions.meaning: a menial non-combat task given to a soldier

explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue means exhaustion and also a soldier's menial duty, often in the plural.

indicators.note: composition suggests the letters of D minor are composed into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece in D minor written by Edward Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' looks like the musical piece but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the famous ninth movement of Elgar's Enigma Variations, a work by that composer.

parts.note: reads like a brief betrothal but means a brief fight between small forces

explanation.surface: A betrothal that is quickly broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' suggests a promise of marriage, but it is a military clash.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a brief minor fight, a short military engagement.

parts.note: L is the learner sign, standing for a student
lots means many

explanation.surface: A university student receives plenty of grants.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to give out or assign, so grants is a present-tense synonym.

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of Cyril are strangely arranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A peculiar poem written by a man named Cyril.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing feeling, of which an ode is one kind.

parts.note: without locks of hair, so bald

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of shared are put out of order

explanation.surface: Smugglers opened up and divided a stash of illicit liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlocked' looks like opening a door but means having no locks of hair. 'Moonshine' is not liquor here but nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean foolish talk, and balderdash is nonsense.

definitions.meaning: a fit of sulking or bad temper, as in in a pet

explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a fit of temper and also a passing fashion, as in all the rage.

indicators.note: disturbing suggests the letters of adders are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fears upsetting snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly, a present-tense match for is afraid of.

clue.text: Nothing clear may come from this prophet

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: may come from suggests a new word is formed out of the letters of clear

explanation.surface: A seer whose sayings are never plain.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a prophet or seer who foretells the future.
